_what: Role recipes: the SQL that makes a login of a kind in the person's own database, gives it its rights, and takes it away. Each statement is a format() string of the server's own (%1$I the role, %2$L its password, %3$L the time it stops working, %4$I the database the connection names), filled by the server so no value is ever spliced into SQL text here. The owner login runs them (it needs CREATEROLE: tools/start-a-computer set-up-postgres-role.sh PG_MAKES_ROLES=yes), in one transaction, so a recipe makes all of a role or none of it. Standing: valid until infinity, the password the person holds under a name. Minted: a made-up password and a VALID UNTIL time; the answer hands the login once.

read-only._what: A login that may connect to the owner's database and read every table of its public schema, the ones there now and the ones the owner makes later, and may do nothing else: a share that may only read.
create: CREATE ROLE %1$I LOGIN PASSWORD %2$L VALID UNTIL %3$L
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO %1$I
drop: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE SELECT ON TABLES FROM %1$I
REVOKE SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
